metadata.note: The Providence and Worcester Railroad (1844/1845) ran Providence - Woonsocket - Worcester itself from 1847 until it was leased to the New York, Providence and Boston ('Stonington Line') on 1 May 1888 and to the New York, New Haven and Hartford from 17 Dec 1892. Passenger trains ended with the State of Maine Express on 29 Oct 1960; the P&W resumed independent operation in 1973 as a freight road that has run occasional excursions since. This layer draws the main line in three operator-era features sharing one geometry (Rule 4), the New Haven's 1893-1896 East Providence - Phillipsdale passenger service, the two Massachusetts roads the P&W operated under lease (Milford and Woonsocket 1868-1883, Hopkinton Railroad 1872-1883), and a one-year [ANCHOR] for the 1984 Boat Train excursions. Research report: research/branches/providence_and_worcester_railroad.txt.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_and_Worcester_Railroad -- Wikipedia, 'Providence and Worcester Railroad' (Featured Article; cites Karr 2017, Lewis 1973)
https://nashuacitystation.org/history/providence-and-worcester-railroad-company/ -- Nashua City Station corporate timeline (lease dates)
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/southernnewenglandrrs2.pdf -- John Fowler, Southern New England Railroads (2), lines 64, 68, 76, 80

metadata.operator_split: Main line: P&W 1847 - 1 May 1888 | New York, Providence and Boston (Stonington Line) 1888 - 17 Dec 1892 | New Haven 1892 - 1960, three features with identical geometry. East Providence Branch: New Haven only (1893-1896). Milford & Woonsocket and Hopkinton RR: P&W colour for the lease years only. The post-1973 P&W (the same corporate shell, re-incorporated 1969) keeps the P&W colour for the 1984 excursion. New colours: P&W #1F4FD4, NYP&B #70B735 (neither company had a feature in data/); New Haven #7209B7 pulled from existing features.
omitted: Phillipsdale - Valley Falls part of the East Providence Branch: no confirmed passenger year (report block [5]; Fowler doubts it).
Bellingham Junction - Woonsocket in the Milford & Woonsocket lease years (block [7], drawable NONE): no source says P&W trains ran it.
Blackstone Valley Polar Express from Woonsocket, c.2000 - 2025 (block [11], drawable NONE): turnaround point not sourced.
Other P&W charters and excursions since the 1980s, incl. Plainfield CT 2012 (block [12], drawable NONE): no dated routes.
1984 Boat Train continuation Providence - New London: routing not confirmed from the article.
Milford & Woonsocket and Hopkinton RR after 1883 (M&W, NY&NE, New Haven) - other companies' eras, left for their own reports.
Worcester - Pratts Junction continuation in Fowler line 76: not a P&W service (report UNRESOLVED 8).

Freight-only (Rule 1): the main line after 29 Oct 1960; the East Providence Branch 1874-1893 and after 1896; the Fox Point waterfront tracks; the whole modern P&W freight network (1973 - ); the proposed Boston Surface Railroad, which never ran trains.
metadata.existing_layer_note: No earlier layer drew the P&W main line, the East Providence Branch, the Milford & Woonsocket or the Hopkinton Railroad (report EXISTING LAYER CHECK, re-checked). boston_and_providence_railroad.geojson draws the shared Providence - Boston Switch track for the B&P; its geometry is reused here, not edited.
not_yet_sourced: All headways and average speeds are estimates; the only train counts are c.1900 (7-8 round trips), 1919 (15 trains/day), 1935 (one each way), 1953 (four each way), 1954 (one round trip).

Last local Providence - Worcester: 1954 confirmed; sources say by 1957 (WPW/Karr), 1956 (Shoreliner index) and 1960 (WBS, WUX). The New Haven feature runs 1954-1960 for the State of Maine Express only.
Stonington Line lease boundaries: 1888 vs 1889 start, 1892 vs 1893 end (NCS day-precise dates used).
East Providence Branch passenger start: 1893 (Karr) vs 1887 (Fowler); 1893 drawn. Exact East Providence station site not established.
Who ran Bellingham Junction - Woonsocket trains 1868-1883; months of the 1868 M&W opening and the 1883 lease expiries.
1984 Boat Train: number of trips, Worcester boarding point, route beyond Providence, other years.
Polar Express route extent and operator (not drawn).
P&W Green Street (Worcester) terminal geometry before 1875 - not drawn (see geometry_quality).

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-16), routed with opstrace.py: Boston Switch (Central Falls) - Worcester on the active P&W main line (OSM ways operator='Providence and Worcester Railroad'; no old_railway_operator tag on this line - 'P&W'/'PW'/'Providence and Worcester' spellings probed and absent). Providence - Boston Switch copied from the existing bp-main-line-central-falls feature (boston_and_providence_railroad.geojson): OSM NEC plus OpenHistoricalMap way -200076833 (1849 Cushing and Walling map) into the 1848 Union depot site. OpenHistoricalMap way -200053744 ('Providence and Worcester Railroad', 1847) for the Boston Switch join and the Worcester terminal point, and as a check on the whole trace.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 43.3 mi against 43.3 mi documented (WPW station table from Karr pp.166-167; Fowler agrees: Providence - Worcester Union Station). Made of: Providence - Boston Switch 4.99 mi (documented MP 4.9), the existing B&P feature's geometry reversed; Boston Switch join 0.36 mi on three OpenHistoricalMap nodes (way -200053744) ending in a c.205 m link to OSM track; Boston Switch - Worcester 37.7 mi on OSM P&W track; final 0.27 mi is OpenHistoricalMap's own last leg (one straight OHM segment) to its Worcester terminal point at Washington Square. No straight-line approximation beyond those two short OHM links. Check: OpenHistoricalMap's 1847 'Providence and Worcester Railroad' way (traced from late-19th-century survey sheets) lies a mean 5 m and at most 18 m from the drawn line over its full 38.3 mi, so the 19th-century alignment survives as today's track. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTES: (1) Providence: the present NEC through downtown Providence is a 1980s relocation and is NOT drawn; the last 1.3 mi follows OHM's 1849-map approach to the 1848 Union depot at Exchange Place (the 1898 Union Station is taken to stand on or beside the same Exchange Place site, so the same end is used for 1898-1986 trains; an inference, not checked against an era map). (2) Through Pawtucket - Central Falls the line is drawn on the present NEC right of way, rebuilt several times since 1847 (joint Pawtucket-Central Falls station 1916). (3) Worcester: the drawn end is the 1875/1911 Union Station approach at Washington Square. Before 1875 P&W trains used their own Green Street station, about 0.6 mi beyond South Worcester (Fowler: 'Former route until 1875'); that pre-1875 terminal leg is not in OSM or OHM and is not drawn, so for 1847-1875 the last c.0.6 mi is a later alignment than the era's.

segments.note: The Providence and Worcester's own operation. Providence - Millville opened 27 Sep 1847 and the rest to Worcester 20 Oct 1847 (WPW, citing Karr p.167). The P&W built the Providence approach, shared with the Boston and Providence from Boston Switch (Central Falls), and its Providence Union Station opened 1848. Fowler's Pathfinder snapshots x=1850 and y=1876 put trains at nearly every station on the line. Ends 1 May 1888, when the New York, Providence and Boston ('Stonington Line') took a 99-year lease (NCS; WPW citing Lewis 1973) - service continued under the lessee (feature pw-main-line-stonington-era). Until 1875 the Worcester terminal was the P&W's Green Street station (see geometry_quality). Headway is an estimate: no P&W-era train count was found.
sources: Segment-level: research report research/branches/providence_and_worcester_railroad.txt block [1] - opening dates from WPW (Karr p.167), lease date 1 May 1888 from NCS and WPW (Lewis 1973 pp.33-35), Fowler line 76 x=1850 / y=1876 station snapshots. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Providence - Worcester under the New York, Providence and Boston Railroad ('Stonington Line'), lessee from 1 May 1888 to 17 Dec 1892 (NCS). Operations 'were changed little, apart from integration with the P&W's new lessee as the Worcester Division' (WPW, Lewis pp.33-35). SOURCE CONFLICTS on the boundary years, recorded not resolved: start 1888 (NCS, WPW) vs 1889 (WEPB; NCS summary field); end 17 Dec 1892 (NCS; WPW 'four years later') vs 1893 (WNYPB, probably the NYP&B's own lease to the New Haven). Service was continuous either way; only the colour boundary moves. No Fowler snapshot falls inside 1888-1892. Headway is an estimate, interpolated from the 7-8 round trips WBS gives for c.1900.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [2] - NCS (1 May 1888 and 17 Dec 1892 lease dates), WPW (Lewis 1973 pp.33-38). Conflicting: WEPB, WNYPB, WBS. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: New York, New Haven and Hartford, lessee of the P&W from 17 Dec 1892 (NCS) to 1968; passenger trains on the line ended with the last State of Maine Express on 29 Oct 1960 (WSME). Local trains Providence - Woonsocket - Worcester. WBS gives 7-8 Providence-Worcester round trips via Blackstone at the turn of the century; Fowler snapshots z (1893/94) and a (1904) at nearly every station. Headway is an estimate derived from that train count.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [3] - NCS (17 Dec 1892 lease), WBS (c.1900 train count, Karr pp.167-168), Fowler line 76 (z, a). Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: New York, New Haven and Hartford, lessee of the P&W from 17 Dec 1892 (NCS) to 1968; passenger trains on the line ended with the last State of Maine Express on 29 Oct 1960 (WSME). WPW (Karr) gives 15 passenger trains a day in 1919; Fowler snapshots b (1920) and c (1932) along the line. Service fell to one train each way by 1935 (next segment). Headway is an estimate from the 1919 count.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [3] - WPW (Karr pp.167-168: 15 trains/day in 1919), Fowler line 76 (b, c). Headway is an estimate.

sources: Segment-level: research report block [3] - WPW and WBS (Karr p.168: one train each way by 1935).

segments.note: New York, New Haven and Hartford, lessee of the P&W from 17 Dec 1892 (NCS) to 1968; passenger trains on the line ended with the last State of Maine Express on 29 Oct 1960 (WSME). From 1946 the overnight State of Maine Express (New York - Providence - Worcester - Portland) used the P&W route, non-stopping on it (WPW, Karr p.168). Locals continued alongside: four each way were tried in 1953 and cut to one round trip in 1954 (WPW, Karr p.168); Fowler snapshot d (1953) at nearly every station. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: research report blocks [3] and [4] - WPW (Karr p.168: 1946 State of Maine Express routing; 1953 four locals; 1954 one round trip), Fowler line 76 (d = 1953). Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: New York, New Haven and Hartford, lessee of the P&W from 17 Dec 1892 (NCS) to 1968; passenger trains on the line ended with the last State of Maine Express on 29 Oct 1960 (WSME). Drawn to 1960 for the State of Maine Express only, which ran over the line until its last trip on 29 Oct 1960 (WSME; WPW: its end left 'no passenger trains on the line'). The LAST LOCAL is NOT claimed here: 1954 is the last year a source positively puts a local on the line, and sources conflict on when locals ended - 'discontinued by 1957' (WPW, Karr p.168), 'through 1956' (Shoreliner v38 i4 per NHRHTA index summary), 1960 (WBS; WUX, probably conflating the locals with the Express). Freight continued after 1960 under the New Haven, Penn Central and the P&W itself; not drawn.
sources: Segment-level: research report blocks [3] and [4] - WSME (29 Oct 1960 last run), WPW (Karr p.168). Locals' end conflicting: WPW, NHR, WBS, WUX.

properties.line: New York, New Haven and Hartford: East Providence Branch
properties.speed_source: estimated: short local; no timetable read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-16) and OpenHistoricalMap way -200053789 ('Providence and Worcester Railroad', 1887), routed with opstrace.py: OSM 'East Providence Running Track' (operator Providence and Worcester Railroad, old_railway_operator NYNH&H) at Phillipsdale and abandoned NYNH&H-tagged ways to the south, with OHM's 1887 branch geometry for the last stretch into East Providence.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 1.66 mi against c.1.7 mi (derived from WPW branch mileposts 6.45 - 4.71; not a documented figure). No straight-line leg. Drawn from the end of OHM's 1887 branch way at East Providence (41.8241, -71.3804), taken as the East Providence (2nd) station area - the exact station site is not established - to Phillipsdale, the terminus of passenger service in Fowler's 1894 snapshot. The Phillipsdale - Valley Falls part of the branch is deliberately not drawn (no confirmed passenger year). Between Phillipsdale and Waterman Avenue the line follows OSM track still in freight use; the 1890s track arrangement there is not separately documented.

segments.note: Passenger service on the otherwise freight-only East Providence Branch (built 1874 to the East Providence coal docks), East Providence - Phillipsdale. WPW (Karr p.169): it 'briefly saw passenger service between 1893 and 1896'. SOURCE CONFLICT on the start: Fowler's line heading gives '1887 > 1896'; the later 1893 is drawn. Fowler's only snapshot (z = 1894) shows Waterman Avenue and Phillipsdale, with Phillipsdale as the terminus, and he doubts service ran on to Valley Falls - so that leg is omitted. Freight continued (and continues); not drawn. Headway is a guess - the service pattern is unknown.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [5] - WPW (Karr p.169: 1893-1896); Fowler line 80 (1887 > 1896; z = 1894, Phillipsdale terminus). Conflict recorded. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Providence and Worcester: Milford – Bellingham Junction
properties.speed_source: estimated: short branch local; no timetable read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-16), routed with opstrace.py: MBTA 'Milford Running Track' and abandoned ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H (and NYNH&H;CSX).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 3.68 mi against c.3.7 mi documented (Fowler line 68 mileposts, Bellingham Jct 5.1 to Milford 8.8). No straight-line leg beyond a 155 m join along the same track in Milford. Drawn from the north end of the surviving rail in Milford (41 m south of the Upper Charles Trail's start, taken as the Milford station area - the exact depot site is not established) to the junction with the abandoned Charles River Branch at Bellingham Junction. The line is drawn on the surviving (later) track, which follows the 1868 right of way; no realignment is recorded, but none was checked against an era map.

segments.note: The Milford and Woonsocket Railroad, opened 1868 and 'immediately leased by the P&W' (WMS) 'to forestall competition' (WPW) - so the P&W ran it, and it carries the P&W colour. The lease expired 1883 (WMS; WPW, Karr pp.370-372); months unknown. Fowler y = 1876 at Milford and Bellingham puts trains here inside the lease; NCS holds an 1874 joint 'Providence & Worcester and Milford & Woonsocket' pass. Passenger traffic focused on Milford - Woonsocket (WMS), but whose trains ran on from Bellingham Junction to Woonsocket over the Charles River line is unresolved, so that leg is not drawn. After 1883 the line was run by the M&W itself, the NY&NE (1887) and the New Haven - other companies, not drawn here. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [6] - WMS (1868 opening and lease, 1883 expiry), WPW (Karr pp.370-372), Fowler lines 64/68 (y = 1876). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Providence and Worcester: Hopkinton Railroad (Milford – Ashland)
properties.speed_source: estimated: branch local; no timetable read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-16): Upper Charles Trail (Milford) routed with opstrace.py, then abandoned / razed / demolished railway fragments (mostly old_railway_operator=NYNH&H) and the Kelleigh and Trolley Brook trails chained by hand Milford - Hopkinton - Ashland. OpenHistoricalMap has nothing in this corridor.
properties.geometry_quality: Drawn 11.8 mi against c.11.4 mi documented (Fowler line 68 mileposts, Milford 8.8 to Ashland 20.2), about 4% long. The grade is mostly lost (north of Hopkinton abandoned 1938), so it is pieced together from OSM fragments with STRAIGHT-LINE JOINS where none survive, 2.86 mi in all: Upper Charles Trail north of Echo Lake - Hayden Row road crossing 0.37 mi; Hayden Row 0.73 mi (42.1908 - 42.2010 N); 0.19 mi at 42.216 N; south of Hopkinton village 0.60 mi (42.2170 - 42.2255 N); 0.21 mi at 42.241 N; final approach into Ashland 0.40 mi (42.2549 - 42.2599 N, to the B&A junction); plus seven joins of 40-125 m totalling 0.34 mi. Milford start is the north end of surviving rail at Milford, shared with feature pw-milford-woonsocket (station site not established); the first 3.2 mi follow the Upper Charles Trail on the grade. Fragments are tagged as the New Haven's (the later owner); they are taken to be the 1872 Hopkinton Railroad grade, as no other railroad ran Milford - Hopkinton - Ashland, but they were not checked against an era map.

segments.note: The Hopkinton Railroad opened between Milford and Ashland in December 1872 and 'was immediately leased by the P&W' (WMS); the P&W lease expired 1883 (WPW, Karr pp.370-372), and the Milford and Woonsocket took the Hopkinton over the following year. P&W-operated, so P&W colour. Fowler y = 1876 at Hayden Row, Hopkinton and Ashland falls inside the lease. Later service (M&W, NY&NE, New Haven; mixed train only from 1914) belongs to other companies and is not drawn. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: research report block [8] - WMS (Dec 1872 opening and lease), WPW (Karr pp.370-372: 1883 expiry), Fowler line 68 (y = 1876). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Providence and Worcester: Boat Train (Worcester – Providence)
properties.speed_source: estimated; no running time known. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-16), routed with opstrace.py: Boston Switch (Central Falls) - Worcester on the active P&W main line (OSM ways operator='Providence and Worcester Railroad'; no old_railway_operator tag on this line - 'P&W'/'PW'/'Providence and Worcester' spellings probed and absent). Providence - Boston Switch copied from the existing bp-main-line-central-falls feature (boston_and_providence_railroad.geojson): OSM NEC plus OpenHistoricalMap way -200076833 (1849 Cushing and Walling map) into the 1848 Union depot site. OpenHistoricalMap way -200053744 ('Providence and Worcester Railroad', 1847) for the Boston Switch join and the Worcester terminal point, and as a check on the whole trace.
properties.geometry_quality: Same geometry as the main-line features: 43.3 mi traced against 43.3 mi documented; see pw-main-line-pw-era for its make-up and the OSM/OHM ways used. For 1984: the Providence end is the pre-1986 approach to the 1898 Union Station, which Amtrak still used in 1984 (the NEC relocation and the new station opened 1986), so it is era-appropriate; but where the 1984 excursions boarded in Worcester (Union Station was closed 1972-2000) and where they joined Amtrak's line in Providence are not known - the ends are approximations. The continuation to New London is not drawn.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] The P&W's 1984 'Boat Train' excursions from Worcester to Providence (and on to New London), per the NHRHTA index summary of Shoreliner v15 i3 (1984), "'The Boat Train' Returns". Only the index summary was read: the number of trips, the exact route beyond Providence and whether they ran in other years are unknown. 1984 is the one confirmed year - excursions may well have run in other years (WPW: P&W has run chartered passenger trains since the 1980s), but none is confirmed, so do not widen this span without evidence. Only Worcester - Providence is drawn. Headway is nominal (a handful of excursion trips).
sources: Segment-level: research report block [10] - NHR (Shoreliner v15 i3 index summary, 1984). General context only: WPW (excursions since the 1980s).
